title: CHALLENGE
text:
the five cases and the intended reading:

• A 28-day strength of 91 MPa — Real. High-performance mixes reach this. Keep it, and check the mix design confirms it.

• A building using 4 kWh per square metre per year — Arguable. A genuine passive house can approach this; so can a building that stood empty all year. You cannot tell from the data alone — and saying so is the correct answer.

• A crack width of -0.4 mm — Error. A width cannot be negative. Almost certainly a sign convention or a data-entry slip.

• An inspection dated 14 months in the future — Error. Someone typed the wrong year.

• A slab 2.5 m thick — Arguable. Wrong for a suspended floor slab, entirely normal for a raft foundation or a mass-concrete pour. Check what structure it belongs to before deleting it.

Mark the reasoning. Make each team commit publicly before you reveal anything.

title: OUTLIER JUDGEMENT
text: this framework is what the challenge is assessed against. Hand it out or leave it on screen during the challenge.

title: CHALLENGE
text:
the five cases and the intended reading:

• A current spike at motor start-up — Real. Inrush current is six to eight times running current and it is physics. Deleting it hides normal behaviour.

• A winding temperature of 200 degrees — Arguable. Beyond every insulation class, so either the motor was destroyed or the sensor failed. Which one changes what you do.

• Vibration of exactly 0.00 for six hours — Error. A real sensor is never exactly zero. This is a dead channel reading as good news, which is the most dangerous defect on this list.

• A negative power reading — Arguable. An error on a motor; entirely correct on a regenerating drive or an inverter exporting to the grid.

• 30,000 rpm on a four-pole induction motor — Error. The synchronous speed at 50 Hz is 1,500 rpm. A decimal point or a unit is wrong.

Mark the reasoning. Make each team commit publicly before you reveal anything.
